function_question: How does nature separate salt from water?

opening.text: There was a girl called Maya who lived in a small island village, where everyone's water came from a few old wells.
Maya helped her neighbours carry water home and checked the wells with the village water team.
The water team's meter showed that the biggest well was turning salty, and it was getting worse every week. "If the wells turn to seawater," Maya said, "what will we drink?"

card.problem: The island's wells are turning salty
card.goal: Make fresh water from salt water using only the sun (a demo, not for drinking)
card.rules: Sun power only. Measure in ml. Never drink or taste the results.

guide.brief: I'm Popi, your story guide. Maya's island wells are turning salty, and the village needs a backup plan fast. Can you help her make fresh water with only the sun? Let's start!
guide.your_idea: Some scientists already have a hunch about how to split salt from water. Do you?
guide.nature_clues: Nature takes salt out of water every day, no factory needed. Tap each card to meet four salt separators!
guide.design_secret: Here's the secret all four heroes share…
guide.skill: Predict first: will the dish on black paper or on white paper lose more water in 2 hours? Change only one variable.
guide.sketch: Draw your still cut in half, with arrows for sunlight, vapour and drops, like a real engineer!
guide.build_and_test: Build your still and a shade control, then measure the ml after 2 hours. Remember: science water only, never for drinking!
guide.retry_tip: Engineers never stop at round 1. Change ONE thing, like a darker base or a wider bowl, and compare your ml.
guide.ending: And ever since then, Maya's village has kept a sun-powered backup still, a rainwater plan to refill the wells, and a data table that started with your experiment.

quick_check.question: Seawater has about 35 g of salt in every litre. How much salt is in 200 ml of seawater?
quick_check.right: Right! 200 ml is one fifth of a litre, and 35 ÷ 5 = 7 g. That's more than a teaspoon of salt in one glass!
quick_check.wrong: Not quite. 1 litre is 1,000 ml, so 200 ml is one fifth of a litre.

clue_cards.name: Red mangrove
clue_cards.trick: Ultra-fine filters in the outer layers of its roots.
clue_cards.does: They let water in but block more than 90% of the salt.

clue_cards.name: Albatross
clue_cards.does: They pull extra salt from its blood and drip it out of its beak.

clue_cards.name: Sea ice
clue_cards.trick: Growing ice crystals have no room for salt.
clue_cards.does: Salty brine is squeezed out, so old ice is nearly fresh.

clue_cards.name: Leaf
clue_cards.trick: Sunlight evaporates water from tiny pores.
clue_cards.does: Only pure water leaves as vapour; the minerals stay behind.

predict.prompt: Does the salt stay behind or travel with the water? Predict first!

items.label: A puddle of seawater drying in the sun
Salt water poured through a paper towel

predict.explain: When water evaporates or freezes, the water molecules leave and the salt is left behind. A paper towel can't stop salt: dissolved salt particles are smaller than a millionth of a millimetre, far smaller than the towel's holes.

lab.title: The evaporation lab
lab.predict: Leave 50 ml of salt water in the sun for 2 hours. Which dish will lose the most water?
lab.measure: ml of water evaporated in 2 hours

tool.name: 5 Whys
tool.intro: You already know the 5 Whys detective tool. Today you'll use all 5 whys on a real crisis, because a still is only a backup until you find the root cause.
tool.example_object: a phone that dies by lunchtime

parts.name: Why #1
parts.example: 📱 Why does it die by lunch? The battery drains fast.
parts.starter: Why are the wells turning salty? Because seawater is…

parts.name: Why #2
parts.example: 📱 Why does it drain fast? The screen is always at full brightness.
parts.starter: Why is seawater getting in underground? Because the fresh water layer…

parts.name: Why #3
parts.example: 📱 Why full brightness? Auto-brightness is switched off.
parts.starter: Why is the fresh water layer shrinking? Because people pump…

parts.name: Why #4
parts.what: Keep digging: don't stop at the easy answer.
parts.example: 📱 Why is it off? It got switched off during a game last week.
parts.starter: Why do people pump more than the rain puts back? Because…

parts.name: Why #5
parts.what: Reach the root cause, then fix that.
parts.example: 📱 Root cause: one setting. Switch auto-brightness back on, no new battery needed!
parts.starter: So the root cause is… and the village could fix it by…
